summary: You pick the Academic MS, Coterminal MS or Honors Cooperative track. The audit checks the core courses (letter graded; BMDS 212 is in the Academic and Coterminal tracks), 18 units of CS, statistics, math and engineering including CS 161, STATS 200 and STATS 315A or CS 229 (at most 9 units below the 200 level, and at most 8 units taken pass/fail), 4 units of social and ethical issues, and your track's unrestricted electives (11 units, or 14 for HCP). Your graduate units must reach 45 at Stanford, with at least 23 units at the 200 level or above and 24 letter-graded units. You check the 3.0 GPA, the advisor-approved program of study and, in the Academic track, the research paper by hand.

BXtSDlqu.why: "Unrestricted Units: 11 units for Academic + Coterm MS students; 14 units for Honors Coop. These can be any graduate-level courses at Stanford at or above the 100 level". With it, what differs by track: "Core Courses (12 units for Academic + Co-term MS; 9 units for Honors Coop)" (BMDS 212), "MED 255 is required only for Academic MS and PhD students", and "All students in the Academic MS program must engage in biomedical data-science-related research ... students must write a research paper reviewed and approved by two faculty members" (research is optional for coterminal students). The coterminal note says coterm students follow the HCP requirements, but the core and unrestricted headings name Academic + Co-term together; the headings are used.
